question.problem: An object moves along a circular path with position $r(t)=\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡4t\,i+\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡4t\,j$ meters. Find the speed of the object at time $t,$ measured in seconds.
question.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

First, we find the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =(r(t))^{′} \\  & =(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡4t\,i+\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡4t)^{′} \\  & =-4\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡4t\,i+4\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡4t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the speed, we calculate the magnitude of the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}||v(t)|| & =\sqrt{(-4\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡4t)^{2}+(4\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡4t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{48{sin}^{2}⁡4t+48{cos}^{2}⁡4t} \\  & =\sqrt{48({sin}^{2}⁡4t+{cos}^{2}⁡4t)} \\  & =4\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the speed of the object is $4\sqrt{3}\text{ m/s}.$

Note that the speed is constant, but the velocity is not. 

**Method 2**

For uniform circular motion in the $xy$-plane, we have

$$
||v||=R|\omega |,
$$

where $R$ is the radius of the circle, and $\omega $ is the angular velocity.

In our case, the radius of the circle is $R=\sqrt{3}\,\text{m}$ and the angular frequency $\omega =4\,\text{rad/s}.$ Therefore,

$$
||v||=\sqrt{3}\cdot |4|=4\sqrt{3}\text{ m/s}.
$$
